extracted.intended_audience: Congressional committee members, oversight investigators, policymakers, Volkswagen executives, dealers, and affected consumers
extracted.subtask_description: Transcript of Volkswagen executive testimony before a House committee about the emissions/deception scandal; contains questions and expectations from members about company actions, transparency, remediation, and consumer/Regulator communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide internal probe documents to the committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Members asked Volkswagen to provide preliminary findings and internal probe documents referenced in news reports to the committee (e.g., 'The Steering Committee ... met last Wednesday to discuss preliminary findings of an internal probe into the scam.' 'Can you get a copy of it and share it with our committee?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where feasible, obtain and share internal investigation reports and supporting documents with oversight bodies to provide clarity into facts and issues; if documents are controlled by supervisory boards or foreign entities, explain constraints and timelines for sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to full cooperation with investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee sought a commitment from VW leadership for 'full cooperation in finding and addressing the roots of the deception.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly and under oath, senior executives should commit to cooperating with regulators and congressional investigations, including providing access to witnesses, documents, and answers to follow-up questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify affected customers promptly and accessibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Members repeatedly asked whether customers had been notified (e.g., owners of 2012/2013 vehicles) and noted instances where owners had received no letters despite being affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customer notification should be timely, direct (mail/email), and not rely on owners disassembling engines; provide clear instructions and provenance so even non-technical owners can confirm whether their vehicle is affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an easy VIN lookup for affected vehicles
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to implement a simple website where owners can enter their VIN and learn if their car is affected and whether it is Generation 1 or Generation 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer an online VIN lookup tool classifying affected vehicles and indicating the applicable remediation pathway; make the tool easy to find and publicize widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish affected vehicle generations and explain remediation complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee members asked VW to confirm whether a 2012 Passat was Generation 2 and noted that fixes for Generation 2 were 'simpler' than for Generation 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate clearly which model years/engine generations are affected and describe differences in proposed fixes and expected impacts on performance and cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore consumer trust through buyback or fair compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: A member urged VW to 'come up with a program that buys these cars back' or otherwise 'stand behind your vehicle' and compensate owners at 'what the fair market value of that vehicle was prior to this notice coming out.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider buyback programs or equivalent remediation that restore consumers to the position they expected pre-disclosure; communicate criteria for valuation and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be transparent and honest with shareholders about liabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Members criticized VW for underestimating potential costs and urged honesty to shareholders (e.g., 'be honest to your shareholders. Six point five billion euros is off by an order of magnitude').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose reasonable estimates and assumptions used to calculate reserves for liabilities; avoid downplaying potential exposures and update investors as investigations and remediation costs become clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with regulators internationally and share findings
rubrics_metrics.description: VW was urged to 'work with those agencies, also with the German KBA' and to collaborate with EPA, CARB and European authorities investigating the issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate remediation, testing, and disclosures with domestic and foreign regulators; provide regulators with technical data and participate in joint validations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate testing and fixes with real-world (on-road) testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns were raised that company testing may rely on dyno tests and not replicate on-road emissions (e.g., Oxnard facility 'didn't do independent road tests'—they 'tested the dyno situation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that validation includes on-road testing and independent verification to detect defeat devices or discrepancies between lab and real-world performance; be transparent about testing methodology and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a thorough internal investigation into who, how, and why
rubrics_metrics.description: Members repeatedly asked VW to investigate how the deception occurred, who made decisions, and whether the problem extended beyond 'a couple of rogue engineers'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Launch and publicize independent internal investigations that trace decision-making, oversight failures, and systemic incentives; provide findings to regulators and oversight bodies as permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure corporate governance accountability and personal responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Quoting a supervisory board member: 'These people ... they’re acting criminally. They must take personal responsibility.' Members pressed for accountability beyond low-level suspensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and, where appropriate, discipline or refer for prosecution those responsible at all relevant levels; explain steps taken to reform governance and oversight structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear explanations to consumers about recall purpose and expected effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee asked 'what explanation was given to consumers about why that December 2014 recall was necessary?' and requested copies of consumer communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer notices should plainly explain why a recall is issued, what part of the vehicle is affected, what corrective measures will be undertaken, any impacts on performance, timelines, and remedies if repairs are unsatisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support dealers and employees affected economically
rubrics_metrics.description: Members described dealers as harmed by the scandal and urged support for dealers and employees who face lost sales and reputational damage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include dealer relief measures (financial or operational support), clear indemnities where appropriate, and proactive engagement with dealer networks to maintain service capacity and consumer trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit not to shift settlement burdens to taxpayers via tax loopholes
rubrics_metrics.description: A member asked VW to commit 'under oath' not to use tax loopholes (as BP allegedly did) to shift settlement costs to taxpayers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make public commitments about tax treatment of remediation costs where possible and ensure settlements do not result in indirect taxpayer subsidies; disclose tax positions related to remediation funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose who represented the company to regulators and the timeline of awareness/actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Members asked who at VW interacted with EPA/CARB, when VW first became aware of research identifying on-road emissions, and what steps were taken thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chronological disclosures of when internal teams learned of external research, who engaged with regulators, what analyses were performed, and how decisions on recalls/fixes were made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate that proposed fixes actually bring vehicles into compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee questioned whether fixes implemented (December 2014 recall) resolved the higher on-road emissions problem and asked for validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish or share test data (lab and real-world) showing before/after emissions performance, and allow independent verification where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accessible point-of-contact and responsive follow-up to committee requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the hearing, members requested follow-up information ('If you could just provide us with that?', 'I can definitely try, sir') and copies of documents to be provided next week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate liaisons for oversight inquiries, commit to timelines for providing requested documents, and follow up proactively to demonstrate cooperation and transparency.
